name: Menemen (Turkish-Style Scrambled Eggs With Tomatoes, Onions, and Chilies)

cookwares.name: medium nonstick or cast iron skillet

ingredients.name: finely diced shishito, Padrón, or Chinese green long pepper

instructions.primary_message: In a medium nonstick or cast iron skillet, heat olive oil over low heat until barely warm. Add paprika, oregano, onion, and peppers. Season with salt and a very generous amount of black pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until very soft, about 8 minutes. Add tomatoes and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until deepened in color. Remove half of mixture and reserve.

Return pan to heat and add beaten eggs. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until eggs are just barely set. Immediately remove from heat and gently fold in reserved vegetable mixture. Sprinkle with chives, if using, and serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: breakfast, brunch, easy, egg, low carb, Mediterranean, quick, turkey, turkish

description: After a week and a half in Turkey, this was the one dish that my sister, my wife, and I were consistently craving. Menemen is a dish of eggs scrambled just until barely set, mixed with tomatoes, chilies, and tons of olive oil. I love to eat it with a side of salty cheese, olives, and some good crusty bread.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano (optional); Minced fresh chives, for garnish (optional; see note)

Optional substitutions: chopped peeled ripe fresh tomatoes → drained canned tomatoes

Notes: If you have access to Aleppo or Urfa chilies, you can use them in place of the paprika for a more authentic flavor. Chives are not traditional in this dish, but I often like to add them because eggs and chives were made for each other; you can opt to include or omit them.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
